full_texts.title: Editorial | The real test begins for the new drug regulator
full_texts.text:
The real test begins for the country’s new drug regulator
Under its new chief, the Centre for Medical Products Regulation must quickly assemble the expertise needed to bridge local strengths with the [another country]’s pharmaceutical power. A [another country]-born former senior official of the US Food and Drug Authority considers the country’s “one country, two systems” governing principle to be a key part of the winning prescription for the new pharmaceutical regulation authority. The other part of the prescription is the strong pharmaceutical industry on the [another country]. 
“The US regulatory body is strong because of its pharmaceutical industry, with both sides pushing each other forward,” he said, noting that the [another country] industry could have a similar symbiotic relationship with the country’s regulator. As a result, while other places in Asia such as a neighbouring country and a regional rival had established regulatory agencies long ago, the country has a distinct competitive edge.

full_texts.title: Fintech Week Wraps Up: AI Solutions Go Global via the Country, Cross-Border Connectivity Accelerates
full_texts.text:
The five-day fintech week x StartmeupHK 2026 concluded on November 6. The event, themed "Fintech Hub: Connecting the World, Building the Future Together," attracted participants from more than 120 economies and over 45,000 attendees, with more than 800 institutions and startups exhibiting. Unlike previous years, the most frequently heard keywords on this year's show floor were "AI deployment" and "going global via the country"—fintech companies are using the country as a dual springboard for product validation and global expansion.

The Director-General of Investment Promotion at the investment promotion authority said the event fostered meaningful connections, partnerships and business opportunities, and that the results will continue beyond the conclusion of the main forum.

AI Agents and Cross-Border Payments Emerge as Two Main Themes
Ant Digital Technologies presented its "AI Agent Super Factory" solution and announced an upgrade to its security brand, launching KYA (Know Your Agent), an identity trust governance solution for the agentic AI era. Ant Digital Technologies CEO said, "AI to B is becoming Ant Digital Technologies' core focus." The solution currently covers industries including finance, energy, healthcare and consumer goods. According to an IDC report, Ant Digital Technologies ranks first among non-cloud vendors and fourth overall in the agent development platform private deployment market.

The Global General Manager of Ant International's WorldFirst said WorldFirst now serves more than 2 million businesses worldwide. Since joining the country's Government's "[another country] Enterprises Going Global Task Force" professional service platform in June this year, the number of companies it serves in going global via the country has grown more than 70% year on year. Ant International also launched a global account service built on AI and blockchain technology, offering one-stop payment, account management, treasury and credit services for large enterprises and cross-border small and medium-sized enterprises based on multi-currency accounts and scenario-based financial solutions.

A major technology company focused on progress in global payment network connectivity. During the event, its global payment service signed memoranda of cooperation with major payment networks, having previously reached a partnership with another. The cross-border remittance platform now cooperates with more than 60 banks and remittance institutions worldwide, supporting remittances to the [another country] from more than 150 countries and regions. The major technology company was also named to the central bank's newly established "Agentic Finance Expert Group," where it will focus on interoperability standards. A Vice President of the major technology company said unified standards and protocols can reduce redundant integration and lower interaction risks.

Self-Evolving Financial Large Model and Cross-Border Data Verification Deployed
A financial technology company, together with a local university and a generative AI research and development center, jointly released a finance-enhanced large model. Built on RSI technology, the model achieves a 30% improvement in core financial scenarios such as customer acquisition, risk control and customer management, at only 10% of the cost of general-purpose models. The financial technology company CEO said the company is the group's international headquarters, and the three parties will jointly promote in-depth AI applications in finance. A Provost of the local university called it the industry's first self-evolving finance-enhanced large model and expressed hope that its deployment in the country will enhance the city's competitiveness as an international financial center.

Another financial technology company focused on exporting digital financial infrastructure. As the country's first digital bank, it has served more than 450 million individual customers and more than 8.4 million corporate customers applying for loans. Its self-developed fully distributed core system handles a peak of more than 1.47 billion financial transactions per day, with product availability exceeding 99.999%, and has deployed more than 100 vertical AI applications and over 90 digital employees.

The cross-border data verification platform showcased by the financial technology company now covers 24 institutions and 13 application scenarios, completing more than 50,000 verifications, facilitating local currency 2.4 billion (approximately $306.1 million) in cross-border credit financing, and providing cross-border medical imaging verification services to more than 10,000 residents. In September this year, the platform was included as a key initiative in the country's first Five-Year Development Plan and the [the country]'s 2026 Policy Address.

Going-Global Paths Gradually Take Shape
The country's value as a hub is particularly evident in the going-global chain. A digital bank empowered by Ant Digital Technologies in a neighbouring country gained 1.2 million users and processed more than 25 million transactions within less than a year of launch. A financial technology company helped a consumer credit institution in another neighbouring country build and upgrade its intelligent credit system and renewed the contract for three years this year. By the first half of 2026, the financial technology company had cooperated with more than 35 enterprises in over ten countries and regions along a major economic initiative, with signed contracts worth over $100 million.

The financial technology company also showcased its intelligent visual anti-fraud strategy platform, which, backed by a million-level Deepfake sample library, achieves end-to-end recognition accuracy exceeding 99%. It has been admitted to the central bank's regulatory sandbox and signed a related construction project with the local police force.

Ecosystem-level cooperation is also expanding in parallel. A major consulting firm and a local technology hub held the annual results day of the Asia-Pacific Fintech Innovation Lab, showcasing solutions from eight startups selected for the 2026 program. A financial index company and the local technology hub launched a one-stop index design solution under the "Thematic Index Exploration Program," using generative AI to improve the efficiency of thematic index development. A fintech association led a delegation of 20 companies to exhibit in the country for the fourth consecutive year.

Market Impact
Judging from the signals sent by this year's fintech week, the going-global path of fintech companies is shifting from single-product exports to a parallel approach of "standards participation plus localized operations." The major technology company's entry into the central bank's agentic finance expert group and the inclusion of the financial technology company's cross-border data verification platform in the country's top-level design mean that these companies' role in the country is no longer merely that of technology suppliers, but of participants in regional rule-making.

For investors, what is worth watching is the change in the revenue structure of such businesses: overseas contracts and localized service revenue at entities such as Ant Digital Technologies and the financial technology company are reaching scale, while the country's validation costs as a "sandbox" remain relatively manageable. IT spending in the financial sectors of emerging markets such as Southeast Asia is expected to maintain a compound annual growth rate of more than 12% through 2030, offering predictable incremental space for companies going global via the country. However, regulatory coordination on cross-border data flows and differing compliance requirements across jurisdictions remain the main variables affecting the pace of deployment.

full_texts.title: Country Forms Team to Support Crypto-Asset Reporting Rules
full_texts.text: The country formed a team to provide technical support and answer industry questions on crypto-asset reporting rules taking effect in 2027. The team will provide technical support and answer industry questions as registration and recordkeeping requirements approach their 2027 start. Providers with a reporting connection to the country will have to register with the tax department and keep due-diligence records under the framework. These requirements are scheduled to start in 2027. Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH) and Solana are generally understood to fall within the rules. The first list of partner jurisdictions will determine which foreign tax authorities can access transaction data from platforms in the country after 2028. The team is one of several arrangements planned to support the framework’s implementation. The development adds an update to the country’s crypto reporting law, which starts collection in 2027.
